question.text: Which of the following entities is NOT eligible for the PAN exemption available for micro investments in mutual funds?

answer.text: An individual investor investing Rs. 40,000 in an equity fund
A Hindu Undivided Family (HUF) investing Rs. 20,000 in a debt fund
An individual investor investing Rs. 50,000 across all schemes of a single fund house
A minor investing through a guardian with an investment of Rs. 10,000

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook exemption from PAN for micro investments (up to Rs. 50,000 in aggregate across all schemes of a fund house) is available only to individual investors. HUFs and other non-individual investors are explicitly ineligible, regardless of the amount invested. The Trap: The HUF's Rs. 20,000 investment is well below the Rs. 50,000 ceiling, but the exemption itself is not extended to HUFs at all. Minors and NRIs sit inside the broader individual-investor category in the source, so they are not analogous to HUFs. Note: Source basis is p.297 (micro-investment PAN exemption limited to individual investors; HUFs and non-individuals not eligible) and p.319 (minors and NRIs described as special categories of individual investors) of the NISM-Series-X-A Investment Adviser (Level 1) workbook (June 2025).
